attempts.label: DANDI:000579
attempts.paper_title: Shared and specialized coding across posterior cortical areas for dynamic navigation decisions
attempts.entry_title: Shared and specialized coding across posterior cortex during navigation decisions (Tseng et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: The behavioral findings largely held up in this data, but most neural findings could not be tested. Performance dropped after rule switches and recovered, strategy shifted toward bias then back to rule-following, and running became more variable, all as reported. Visually guided trials updated rule belief more than normal trials, unlike the paper, and the paper does not describe how the update was computed. The photoinhibition experiments are not in the dataset, and the single-neuron encoding gradients depend on GLM fits that were too large to rerun. Population decoding reproduced the V1-to-A cue gradient, while RSC being most active in the stem held only in part. I did not create `summaries/000579-tseng-2022-01.md`.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Tseng, Chettih, Arlt, Barroso-Luque and Harvey (2022) on dandiset 000579, which holds 300 two-photon imaging sessions of 8 mice running a virtual Y-maze with rule switches. It tests the neuron counts, the behaviour around rule switches, the stored strategy and dynamic-choice models, a refit reinforcement learning model, running trajectories, activity by trial epoch and population decoders fit on a subsample of sessions, with a second notebook that fits the decoders of every V1 and PM field session and of the sessions with the Figure 8C cue offset. The GLM encoding analyses and the shattering dimensionality are beyond the run's time, and the photoinhibition sessions are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Tseng et al. (2022) from dandiset 000579
Population decoders of every V1 and PM field session, and of the sessions with the cue offset at 0.76

outcomes.notes: With session fraction correct over all trials, 150 layer 2/3 sessions above 0.65 hold 97,989 neurons from 8 mice (V1 15,497, PM 10,313, AM 15,225, MM 10,654, RSC 23,728, A 22,572), each within its tolerance; the area shares are within 0.006 of the paper's. With visually guided trials excluded from fraction correct, 100 sessions and 69,707 neurons remain and only the mouse count is within tolerance. The files hold 278,155 neurons in 300 sessions, the paper's total, so the stored sources are the paper's neurons; the paper's list of 141 sessions cannot be recovered.
deviations: Sessions above 0.65 are selected on fraction correct over all trials, an assumption (Methods, Classification of the sources, gives 141 layer 2/3 sessions above 65% correct; Behavioral training says visually guided trials are excluded from all analyses). Only fraction correct over all trials gives counts near the paper's (150 layer 2/3 sessions, 97,989 neurons); with visually guided trials excluded there are 100 and 69,707. Both selections are shown.
The paper's cell-body classifier is not in the files; the stored sources are taken as the cell bodies, since their total equals the paper's 278,155 neurons.

outcomes.notes: Over 601 switches in 297 sessions above 0.5 (fraction correct over all trials), the end of the block before the switch is 0.807, the fitted initial performance after the switch 0.226 ± 0.016 (no bootstrap sample at or above 0.5), the fitted end performance 0.727 ± 0.026, and end minus initial 0.501 ± 0.038 (p < 0.0001). With visually guided trials excluded from the selection, 589 switches give 0.225 and 0.730. The end mean is above 0.7 only just: 15% of bootstrap samples (12% with the other selection) are at or below 0.7, and with the other selection two of the 8 mice end below 0.7 (0.613 and 0.666). With a free sigmoid midpoint the initial value is 0.317. The paper reports 506 to 513 switches. The fit overestimates initial performance a little on synthetic blocks (verifier), which works against the below-0.5 test.
deviations: The sigmoid's t0 is fixed at the block's first trial, as the Methods state (Task performance analysis); a free midpoint is shown as a variant. Rates are kept in (0, 1) by the fit's parametrisation, the claims file's standard choice.
The session selection above 0.5 matches no reading of the paper's 253 sessions (291 or 297 here); both readings are shown and agree.

outcomes.notes: Accuracy of the stored predictions is 0.772 over all 300 sessions (SD 0.064 over sessions; 0.771, SD 0.043 over mice). Above 0.65 it is 0.792 (visually guided excluded from the selection, 154 sessions) and 0.769 (all trials, 238 sessions). Every reading is within 0.051 of 0.802. Per mouse 0.705 to 0.826.
deviations: The LSTM was not refit. The association matrices stored in the trial tables are taken as the paper's held-out (leave-one-session-out) predictions, an assumption, as the files do not say how they were produced; the Methods (LSTM model) describe only held-out predictions being used for analysis.

outcomes.notes: On the 238 sessions above 0.65 (all trials), held-out log2 likelihood per trial is -0.710 for the LSTM and -0.732 for RL model 4; the LSTM is higher in 185 sessions, Wilcoxon p = 4.65e-22 (paper 5.95e-22, 216 sessions). On the 154 sessions of the other selection, -0.667 against -0.691, p = 1.42e-17. The LSTM is ahead in all 8 mice. The optimiser reported convergence for the best of three starts in all 238 folds, and the starts reach the same likelihood in the median fold (spread 0.000, at most 480 of a median 8,262). The learning rate for unrewarded trials is at its lower bound of 0 in 198 folds and the inverse temperature at its upper bound of 50 in 50 folds.
deviations: RL model 4 was refit in Python (L-BFGS-B with bounds, three starting points) in place of Matlab's fminunc, leave-one-session-out over all sessions of each mouse (Methods, Reinforcement learning model). The lapse is the mixture (1 - lambda) P + lambda/2 (claims file), the bias inside the inverse temperature as printed, and visually guided trials update the model but are left out of the likelihood, as for the LSTM.
The LSTM side uses the stored predictions (see lstm-choice-accuracy).

outcomes.notes: Under both windows (10 and 20 trials) and both session selections, rule-following before the switch is 0.23 to 0.26 (p < 1e-4 against zero) with choice bias 0.13 to 0.16; the probability of the actual choice drops by 0.14 to 0.17 (p < 1e-4) with a switch-aligned minimum of 0.570 to 0.578; bias-following rises by 0.029 to 0.045 (p <= 4e-4); rule-following rises from 0.04 to 0.07 in the first window to 0.21 to 0.22 at the end of the block (p < 1e-4). Recovered switches number 320 (all-trial selection) and 251, against the paper's 265.
deviations: Strategy variables are those stored in the files, not refit.
The end of the block is taken as its last W non-visually guided trials; the claims file says only 'by the end of the block'.

outcomes.notes: With the update of trial t taken as rule belief on t + 1 minus that on t (the adopted reading), visually guided trials update more than normal trials over the 30 trials after a switch, 0.0545 ± 0.0075 against 0.0215 ± 0.0029, difference 0.0329, p < 0.0001 (302 switches; the other selection gives 0.0591 against 0.0236, p = 0.0022), so the paper's test finds the effect the claim says is absent. On correct trials only there is no difference (0.068 against 0.076, p = 0.22; paper p = 0.89). The change from t - 1 to t gives no difference (0.0295 against 0.0267, p = 0.48), but it is not the adopted reading and is not taken as support. Correct trials move belief toward the new rule (0.0765 normal, 0.0690 visually guided) and incorrect trials away from it (-0.0243, -0.0129); 80% of visually guided trials are correct against 46% of normal trials, which accounts for the forward difference. Under every all-trial reading both values are 2 to 5 times the paper's 0.013 and 0.0080, outside the tolerances (the correct-only rows, which have no paper values, give 0.076 to 0.080 for normal trials); the stored switch-aligned rule belief itself rises by 0.028 per trial over the 30 trials (from -0.619 to 0.195). The question of how the update was defined is put to the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: Assumed. The Methods (Decision-making strategy variables) do not say which difference of rule belief is a trial's update. The LSTM's belief on trial t is conditioned on trials 1 to t - 1 (Methods, LSTM model), so the change from t to t + 1 is the one trial t causes; this reading is adopted. The change from t - 1 to t is shown.
Rule belief is recomputed from the stored association matrix with the Methods' sign, as the stored column has the opposite sign (findings).

Δ trajectory correlation after minus before the switch is -0.077 ± 0.013 (11 bins) and -0.074 ± 0.012 (20 bins) with the all-trial selection (320 and 317 switches), -0.090 and -0.087 with the other (251 and 248), p < 1e-4 in each, and negative in all 8 mice. Trials with an empty position bin are dropped (1,066 to 2,556 trials).
deviations: Trials with an empty position bin are dropped; the Methods do not say how such trials are handled.

outcomes.notes: The maze epoch matches the legend's trial duration (9.31 ± 2.14 s, all-trial selection; 8.98 ± 1.93 s, the other; expected 8.95 ± 2.04), and trial start_time is maze onset (first frame with a position at median -0.004 s). With the all-trial selection (70,410 trials crossing threshold, paper 85,463), latency falls with rule-following (Spearman rho -0.113; highest against lowest bin p = 0.0045 with 5 bins and p < 0.0001 with 10) and with bias-following (rho -0.102; p = 0.0011 and p < 0.0001). With the other selection every test holds except bias-following with 5 bins (0.587 against 0.656, p = 0.058), so the outcome rests on the session selection; the hierarchical bootstrap with 8 mice is liberal near 0.05 (verifier), so p values near it are fragile. One mouse has a positive rho for rule-following.
deviations: Dynamic choice is the stored velocity LSTM output, not refit.
Trial duration is the maze epoch, the duration that matches the legend's 8.95 s (the whole trial is 14.9 s).
Trials whose dynamic choice never crosses threshold are left out (4,015 of 74,425).

Sessions above 0.65 are selected on fraction correct over all trials, an assumption (Methods, Classification of the sources, gives 141 layer 2/3 sessions above 65% correct; Behavioral training says visually guided trials are excluded from all analyses). Only fraction correct over all trials gives counts near the paper's (150 layer 2/3 sessions, 97,989 neurons); with visually guided trials excluded there are 100 and 69,707. Both selections are shown.

outcomes.notes: In the first position bin the bias-following coefficient is 0.28 to 0.42 (p <= 0.001) and the rule-following coefficient -0.016 to 0.000 (p >= 0.36, at most 0.05 of the bias coefficient); in the last stem bin the rule-following coefficient is 0.85 to 0.90 (p < 0.0001), above its first-bin value (p < 0.0001). Holds for 11 and 20 bins, both session selections, and the local reward rate with or without the current trial.
deviations: Choice commitment uses the stored dynamic choice.

Local reward rate is the fraction correct over the 9 non-visually guided trials centred on the trial (Figure S2L legend says 'adjacent 9 trials'); the 8 neighbours without the trial itself are run as a variant and give the same result.

outcomes.notes: Cue-biased running varies across mice (mean cue log likelihood by mouse -0.92 to -0.36) and in direction across and within mice (roll coefficient positive in 79 of 238 sessions; all 30 negative in mouse 5; 27 positive and 11 negative in mouse 10). Per-mouse slopes of performance on cue decoding are not different from zero (mean 0.024, bootstrap p = 0.35; other selection -0.048, p = 0.35), but the pooled correlation over sessions is positive (r = 0.224, p = 0.0005; other selection r = 0.207, p = 0.010). The criterion's two readings disagree, so the claim holds in part. The Figure S2G part was reported, not judged; choice decoding rises with cue decoding in the third quadrant of the maze, from -0.675 to -0.509 over the 7 bins of cue decoding; in the second it rises from -0.817 to -0.726 over the first four bins and stays at -0.768 to -0.776 in the last three.
deviations: Cue decoding uses the stored cue-biased running. The pooled-correlation and per-mouse readings are the claims file's; the per-mouse test is a bootstrap over mice (the Methods' default), with a t-test shown.
The logistic decoder is fit with scikit-learn (unpenalised in effect, C = 1e6) on z-scored velocities in place of Matlab's fitglm.

outcomes.notes: Two parts of the claim hold and one does not. In the feedback period/ITI RSC is the least active area (-0.042) and A the most (0.023), A above RSC (p < 0.001) in both selections and in all 8 mice; within RSC the feedback period/ITI is the lowest epoch (p < 0.001). RSC is not shown to be most active in the stem: within RSC the arm mean exceeds the stem mean (0.042 against 0.023, p = 0.07; other selection p = 0.18; arm higher in 7 of 8 mice), and between areas RSC's stem mean is the highest and above V1, PM, MM and A (p <= 0.016) but not AM (p = 0.29); with the other selection only PM and A differ. The criterion asks for every comparison under every reading, and the well-fit reading was not run. The verifier would call this not reproduced; it is kept as partially reproduced because two of the claim's three parts hold (see verifications).
deviations: Only the all-neuron reading was run; the well-fit reading of the claims file needs the GLM fits (blocked).

Epochs are taken from the frame-aligned position and time from the choice point in the files: stem below the stem length, arm from there to the choice point (including 913,421 frames just past the 2.5 m maze end), feedback/ITI after the choice point. Frames of the 1 s feedback delay have no position (0 of 3,673,732), so they fall in feedback/ITI.

Sessions above 0.65 are selected on fraction correct over all trials, an assumption (Methods, Classification of the sources, gives 141 layer 2/3 sessions above 65% correct; Behavioral training says visually guided trials are excluded from all analyses). Only fraction correct over all trials gives counts near the paper's (150 layer 2/3 sessions, 97,989 neurons); with visually guided trials excluded there are 100 and 69,707. Both selections are shown.

In the single-plane sessions (13 in the dandiset; 8 of the 150 layer 2/3 sessions of the all-trial selection) the deconvolved activity timestamps run 2000 times the behaviour clock (findings); their frames are matched to behaviour by index, one frame per behaviour frame.

outcomes.notes: Needs the Poisson GLM of the Methods fit to every layer 2/3 neuron (5-fold cross-validation over 21 penalties plus a final fit, 106 fits per neuron). The dandiset holds no fitted coefficients, deviances or encoding strengths. The notebook times one L2 Poisson fit of the median session's training frames by 1,310 predictors at 0.2 s, which puts the 97,989 neurons at 652 CPU hours, a random subsample of 2,000 neurons at 13.3 CPU hours (3.3 h on the run's 4 cores) and one of 200 at 1.3 CPU hours (0.3 h), each a lower bound since the Methods' group lasso is slower. The fit time varies between runs on the same machine type: the round-2 run printed 0.4 s per fit (1,191, 24.3 and 2.4 CPU hours). Even the 200-neuron subsample, 20 to 36 minutes of fitting by these lower bounds, leaves no room in a 30-minute notebook for streaming the sessions and building the design, and 200 neurons give about 33 per area. The design matrix (27 task variables on raised-cosine bases, 336 movement predictors, drift terms) and the predictor grouping are not in the paper's public code. Not run.

V1 and PM come from every decoder of the 41 pool sessions with a V1 or PM field (decoders_v1_pm_offset.ipynb; 149 V1 and 71 PM decoders with k-means groups, 142 and 80 with tiles), the other four areas from the main notebook's 116 decoders of 18 sessions. Cue decoding is held-out log2 likelihood, chance -1. V1 is above PM under all 12 readings, by 0.027 to 0.062 (V1 -0.139 to -0.246, PM -0.187 to -0.282); the difference is significant only for tiles over the stem bins (p = 0.039 and 0.042), p = 0.098 to 0.474 otherwise. The highest of the other areas, AM (-0.276 to -0.382, 16 to 17 decoders in 3 mice), is 0.118 to 0.157 below V1. A is the lowest area in all 12 readings and V1 is above A by 0.355 to 0.409 (p < 0.001). So V1 is the highest area and A the lowest under every reading, with V1 above A at p < 0.05, which the criterion calls reproduced. On the subsample alone V1 was highest in only 2 of 12 readings (PM above V1 by 0.001 to 0.027 on 12 to 14 PM decoders). For k-means groups, frame folds, the minimum penalty and stem bins, the only reading printed per mouse and per field, V1 is above PM in each of the 6 mice with both areas (mouse 3 by 0.012) and within each field. Decoders labelled PM in sessions of other fields are not fitted, so PM has 71 to 80 decoders against the paper's 106; in the subsample such decoders do not average higher than the PM field's. Frame folds and trial folds give the same ranking. Proposed after round 2 and agreed in round 3.
deviations: The decoders were fit on a random subsample of 18 of the 142 multi-plane layer 2/3 sessions of the all-trial selection (3 per imaged field's area, seeded), 116 decoders against the paper's 974, as at the notebook's rate (488 s on 4 processes for the 18 sessions, 108 CPU-s per session) all 142 sessions take about 4.5 CPU hours, 67 minutes on 4 cores, over the 30-minute notebook limit. The 8 single-plane layer 2/3 sessions of this selection (150 - 142) were left out. A second notebook, decoders_v1_pm_offset.ipynb, fits every pool session with a field in V1 or PM (41 sessions, 23,375 neurons, 922 s on 4 processes) and the 6 pool sessions with the cue offset at 0.76.

Decoders follow the Methods (Trial phase-specific logistic decoders): groups of about 100 neurons, PCA to more than 90% of variance, logistic regression with elastic net (10% L1) per each of 11 position bins on single frames (6 Hz volumes), 5-fold cross-validation. The solver is FISTA written here in place of Matlab's lassoglm (checked against scikit-learn's saga to 2e-5), with 10 penalties from the largest useful one down to 1e-4 of it (lassoglm's range, fewer values), a standard choice. Dynamic choice is fit as a binomial proportion.

Readings: penalty at the minimum CV deviance and one-SE; groups by k-means and by equal-count tiles (claims file). The Methods do not say how folds are formed; lassoglm's default (random frames) and folds of whole trials are both run, the latter with k-means groups only. Areas are the label of the neuron nearest each group's centroid (97% agree with the members' majority area).
Frames are maze traversal of non-visually guided trials; stem frames are those below each session's stem length.

Assumed. The Figure 8C legend uses only sessions with the cue offset at 0.76 of the maze. The files' cue delay length gives that offset for 6 of the 142 sessions in the pool and none of the 18 decoder sessions (offsets 0.96 and 1.0), and none with a field in V1 or AM (findings), so the cue test uses every decoder session, with the cue-present bins set by each session's own offset. The 6 sessions with the 0.76 offset are decoded in the second notebook and give the same result.
Cross-position tests use folds of whole trials, so that a test frame never comes from a training trial.

outcomes.notes: Needs pseudo-populations of 1,000 neurons per area resampled 1,000 times, with linear SVCs on every marginally balanced dichotomy of each conjunction, 10 splits each, on stem frames of all layer 2/3 neurons, under two readings of choice. The notebook counts 126 marginally balanced dichotomies for cue by 10 positions alone and times one SVC on 20 conditions by 1,000 neurons at 1.04 ms, which puts that one conjunction at 17,640,000 fits and 5.1 CPU hours (1.3 h on 4 cores; earlier runs printed 0.69 and 0.81 ms, 3.4 and 3.9 CPU hours), a lower bound without building the trial samples and without the other conjunctions of Figure 8G. Not run.

findings.statement: The trial-table column rule_belief equals P(rule A) - P(rule B) in all 300 sessions, recomputed from the stored association matrix, and correlates negatively with the current rule being B (median r -0.73). The paper's Methods and the dataset's tutorial notebook both define it as positive for rule B. The other strategy columns match the Methods' formulas exactly.

In the single-plane sessions the timestamps of the deconvolved activity, labelled seconds, are 2000 times the behaviour clock (for example 25356 against 12.678 s at the first frame), while the planes have exactly one frame per behaviour frame. Matching activity to behaviour by these timestamps puts every frame at the end of the session.

The paper's session counts cannot be recovered from the files. With session fraction correct excluding visually guided trials (the Methods' rule for all analyses) there are 291 sessions above 0.5, 154 above 0.65 and 100 layer 2/3 sessions above 0.65 (69,707 neurons), against the paper's 253, 216 and 141 (93,881 neurons). With all trials there are 297, 238 and 150 (97,989 neurons). Only the last matches the neuron counts within 10%. No file marks which sessions the paper analysed.
The paper says the fraction of visually guided trials typically varied from 0 to 20%; in the files the median session has 23% and 222 of 300 sessions have more than 20% (up to 78%).

The photoinhibition experiments (7 VGAT-ChR2 mice, 164 sessions; Figures 1J to 1M, S1K to S1M, S2M) are not in the dandiset, and the paper names no other archive for them. Three of the paper's findings cannot be tested.

The dandiset holds no GLM fits, encoding strengths or population decoders, on which 29 of the 43 claims rest. Refitting the GLM is estimated at no less than 652 CPU hours (a lower bound timed in the notebook, which varies between runs up to 1,191), so the 24 GLM claims cannot be checked against the deposit without the derived results or far more compute; the decoders were refit here on a subsample of sessions.
7 of 300 sessions have a 150-unit (1.5 m) maze stem where the paper describes a 200-unit stem; the TaskParam metadata records it. The analyses here use each session's own stem length.

Question for the paper's authors. How was the rule update per trial (Δ rule belief) of visually guided and normal trials computed (STAR Methods, Decision-making strategy variables)? Taking it as the change from trial t to t + 1 gives a larger update for visually guided trials (0.055 against 0.022, p < 0.001); from t - 1 to t gives none (0.030 against 0.027, p = 0.48); both give values 2 to 5 times the reported 0.013 and 0.0080.

Question for the paper's authors. Was the 65% session threshold applied to fraction correct over all trials, including visually guided ones? Only that reading comes near the 141 sessions and 93,881 neurons, but it gives 238 sessions where the supplement reports 216, and no reading gives the 253 sessions above 0.5.

The Figure 8C legend has 698 decoders (100 in V1) from sessions with the cue offset at 0.76 of the maze, but the TaskParam cue delay length gives that offset (60 of 250 maze units) for only 8 of the 172 multi-plane layer 2/3 session files and 6 of the 142 in the decoder pool (fields RSC 2, A 2, PM 1, MM 1; 53 decoders), none with a field in V1 or AM; most sessions have a delay of 10 units (offset 0.96) or none. Which variable marks the paper's cue offset is not described.

disagreements.reason: RSC has the highest stem mean of all areas, but it is not significantly above AM (p = 0.28/0.45), nor above V1 or MM under (a). Within RSC, activity is higher in the arm than in the stem (arm higher in 7 of 8 mice). The part that holds: A is above RSC in the feedback period/ITI (p < 1e-3). Only the all-neuron reading was run. It was never checked whether the 1 s feedback delay keeps a position and so falls into the arm, and the frame counts per epoch were not printed.

entries.name: 000579-tseng-2022
entries.title: Shared and specialized coding across posterior cortex during navigation decisions (Tseng et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Tseng, Chettih, Arlt, Barroso-Luque and Harvey (2022) on dandiset 000579, which holds 300 two-photon imaging sessions of 8 mice running a virtual Y-maze with rule switches. It tests the neuron counts, the behaviour around rule switches, the stored strategy and dynamic-choice models, a refit reinforcement learning model, running trajectories, activity by trial epoch and population decoders fit on a subsample of sessions, with a second notebook that fits the decoders of every V1 and PM field session and of the sessions with the Figure 8C cue offset. The GLM encoding analyses and the shattering dimensionality are beyond the run's time, and the photoinhibition sessions are not in the dandiset.
